Ruling: batch #196 item 2 · letter C′ · maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-20T10:21Z

Director seat, summon #25, `session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`. Presented in detail with the recommendation **C′** (the converter aligns to the protocol's refusal set, with B as the fallback for stored documents); the maintainer agreed 「同意」. Thread re-read to its last comment (5724194992) in the act that wrote this. Facts (card + triage, anchors verified by triage): `convertFiltersToAST` carries eleven throw sites; `toFilterNode` delegates to it from four render-time `useMemo` sites (`RelatedList.tsx:505`, `LineItemsPanel.tsx:156`, `ObjectGrid.tsx:1616` / `:1990`); on the query path `classifyLoadError` turns the same throw into 「malformed filter」; in-repo authored metadata shows zero instances, customer-stored documents are unmeasurable from here.

## Ruling — **C′**: the protocol is the only refusal set; render time never throws on a protocol-valid document

1. **Consumer aligns to protocol.** The converter's throw set must be a subset of what `ViewFilterRuleSchema` refuses at parse: every shape the protocol accepts converts; every shape the converter refuses, the protocol refuses first (with its own prescription). Step 1 is the measurement: for each of the eleven throws, does the protocol refuse the same input today? The differences are the protocol's to close — the spec seat files the objectstack card with those readings (ADR-0087 entries where a narrowing refuses authored input that parsed before). ⇒ a document that passed the protocol cannot reach a render-time throw.
2. **B as the fallback for stored documents**: the four render-time callers catch a conversion error and render a visible 「this view's filter is malformed」 state naming the operator, ⛔ never `undefined` (**A refused** — a silently unconstrained query is the failure objectui#9001 just closed). The subtree around the malformed filter keeps rendering.
3. **C (a new save-time gate) is not built**: the protocol's parse is the save-time gate; aligning to it is the whole of C without a second validator.

Four-facet reading (this seat's own): ① one refusal set, declared once, and the runtime never contradicts the declaration; ② exposure is latent in-repo and unmeasurable in customer stores, which is why B stays as the floor; ③ A is silent (worst), C′ refuses loudly at parse, B turns a residual crash into a visible diagnostic; ④ an alignment plus a small render state, no new gate.

`Prior rulings read:` objectui#9001 (the silent-unconstrained-query failure, closed — A is refused on it), objectui#9048 (acceptance axis, adjacent), thread: 1.

## Execution, same stroke

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` stand. Step 1 (measurement) and step 2 (B) are one objectui PR; the protocol-side deltas from step 1 go to an objectstack card filed by the claiming seat at ACCEPT (rule 3, with the readings). `Clause-②` declared from the diff (a render state on published components ⇒ expected `no`; any converter change that widens what converts is `yes`).

Recorded here rather than carried in a session, because 「延后不是搁置 —— 被延后那一刻就把已知的坑记到该 issue 上」.

### ⭐ The reading the next taker most needs, because it moves what step 2 is FOR

The card's body says a render-time throw 「propagates as a render error and takes the subtree down」. **Measured today, that is not what happens on the schema path**:

| measured | site |
|:--|:--|
| `SchemaRenderer` wraps **every** rendered component node in a per-component `SchemaErrorBoundary`, with auto-recover on `resetKey` | `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:2067-2110`; the class at `:624`, its docblock at `:615-617` says so in as many words |
| that boundary's visible result is a per-component banner, ⛔ not a blank page | `plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx:556` and `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:346` both describe hitting it |
| the console ALSO has one route-level `ErrorBoundary` around the whole `<Routes>` block, whose fallback prints `error.message` | `packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:1037-1124`; fallback at `chrome/ErrorBoundary.tsx` |
| CONTROL — no per-subtree boundary of their own in the call sites' own packages | `plugin-grid` **0** non-test `ErrorBoundary` hits, `plugin-form` **0** |

⇒ **on the schema-rendered path the ruling's step-2 goal 「The subtree around the malformed filter keeps rendering」 may ALREADY hold**, via a boundary nobody wrote for this. If so, what B buys is not containment — it is the **named** diagnostic (「this view's filter is malformed: `$regex`」) in place of a generic 「Component failed to render」 banner, which is a real but different deliverable, and it changes what the pin has to discriminate: a pin that only proves 「the page did not blank」 would be **green before the change too**.

⚠️ ⛔ NOT MEASURED, and this is the first thing the claiming seat owes:
1. Which of the four call sites are always reached through `SchemaRenderer`, and which can be mounted directly (`DetailView` imports `RelatedList` itself). A site outside `SchemaRenderer` has no per-component boundary and falls back to the route boundary — or, in a host embedding these packages outside the console, to **nothing**.
2. What the per-component banner actually renders for a `FilterOperatorError` — whether the operator name survives into it or is swallowed.

⛔ None of this reopens C′. Rule 1 (the converter's throw set becomes a subset of what `ViewFilterRuleSchema` refuses at parse) is untouched by any of it, and rule 2's refusal of A (returning `undefined`) is untouched too. It bears only on **what step 2's visible state has to be better than**, and on the pin that proves it.

Filed at the direction of objectui#9050's ruling (comment 5749197961, batch #196 item 2, letter C'), rule 1: "the differences are the protocol's to close". These are the readings from that card's step-1 measurement, taken by the objectui `domain:ui` execution seat on objectui PR #10201.

## How these were measured

Every row below is a `safeParse` against INSTALLED `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 — the published artifact objectui builds and ships against (`@object-ui/core` floor `^17.3.0`) — driven from objectui's own `toFilterNodeSafely` so the converter verdict and the protocol verdict are read on the same input. Envelope controls and negative controls are included below; without them the REFUSE readings are phantoms, which my first pass produced.

## Delta 1 — `ViewFilterRuleSchema` accepts an ARRAY on a single-valued operator, contradicting its own `value` description

Input: `{ field: 'tags', operator: 'equals', value: ['a'] }`
  - `ViewFilterRuleSchema.safeParse(...)` -> ACCEPT
  - objectui's `convertFiltersToAST` (`viewFilterRuleToNode`) -> THROW `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 (objectui#8557)

The schema's own `value` `.describe()` says, verbatim: "The accepted SHAPE depends on the operator: `in` / `not_in` take an array (any length, including []), `between` takes exactly [min, max], every other operator takes a scalar."

The coupling IS implemented — `.superRefine(checkViewFilterRuleValueShape)` (view.zod.ts:724, checker at :602) — and it works for the two classes it covers. Controls, on the same schema and the same artifact:
  - `{ field:'a', operator:'in', value:'x' }` -> REFUSE
  - `{ field:'a', operator:'between', value:[1,2,3] }` -> REFUSE
The checker ends `if (!isPair) return;`, so every operator that is neither a list operator nor `between` is not checked at all.

Why it matters downstream: the lowered node `['tags','equals',['a']]` passes `isFilterAST` and `parseFilterAST` hands back `{ tags: ['a'] }`; `@objectstack/driver-sql` answers 400 INVALID_FILTER and every in-memory matcher excludes every row. So a stored view that PASSED the protocol can select nothing, or (before objectui#10201) reach a render-time throw.

Suggested shape: extend `checkViewFilterRuleValueShape`'s final arm to refuse a non-scalar `value` on the scalar operators, with the same message idiom the two existing arms use. ADR-0087 entry: this narrows what parses today.

## Delta 2 — `ViewFilterRuleSchema` accepts an `icontains` comparand that `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` declares refused

Input: `{ field: 'name', operator: 'icontains', value: '' }`
  - `ViewFilterRuleSchema.safeParse(...)` -> ACCEPT
  - objectui's `viewFilterRuleToNode` -> THROW `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 (objectui#9048)

`@objectstack/spec/data`'s `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` already DECLARES this refusal, as data, in the same package:
  - "an empty $icontains comparand is REFUSED" — `expectRejection: true`, `code: 'INVALID_FILTER'`, `mustMention: ['$icontains']`
  - "a non-string $icontains comparand is REFUSED" — same, for `42`
Those rows are a BACKEND conformance table. Nothing applies them at parse, on either vocabulary: `FilterConditionSchema.safeParse({ name: { $icontains: '' } })` is ACCEPT too. So the platform declares the refusal and then admits the document that will hit it.

Suggested shape: apply the `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` refusal predicate at parse on both doors — the `$`-dialect `FilterConditionSchema` and `ViewFilterRuleSchema`'s `icontains` arm. ADR-0087 entry on both.

## Delta 3 — `ObjectGridPropsSchema.defaultFilters` is `z.unknown().optional()`, so the block's fallback filter key is ungated

Measured on the installed artifact and re-read in `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` (schema opens at :2661):

    objectName:     z.string().optional()              <- control, discriminates (42 REFUSED)
    columns:        z.array(z.unknown()).optional()
    filter:         z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema, {...}).optional()   <- narrowed in this tree
    defaultFilters: z.unknown().optional()             <- UNCONSTRAINED
    sort:           z.array(SortItemSchema).optional()

`defaultFilters` is described as "Legacy base-filter fallback, read only when `filter` is absent", i.e. the SAME value in the same role as `filter` — and `filter` has been narrowed to a `ViewFilterRule` array while its fallback accepts a bare string, a number, or any object. objectui's `ObjectGrid` reads it through the same lowering sink as `filter` (`toFilterNode`), so every one of the eleven refusals is reachable from a document that passed the protocol. This is the one gap on this block that no release closes.

Suggested shape: either narrow `defaultFilters` to the same union the lowering accepts, or — preferable, and consistent with the deprecation already stated in its own description — declare it refused outright with a migration pointing at `filter`. ADR-0087 entry either way.

## Delta 4 (reporting, not a spec defect) — the `filter` narrowing has not reached objectui's floor

The `filter: z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema, ...)` narrowing above is present in the `objectstack` working tree at `04d639c659` but NOT in the published `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 that objectui installs, where the same key reads `z.unknown().optional()` and carries the older `.describe()` ("Base query filter (ObjectQL filter array/AST) ..."). Same version string, different content. So on the tree objectui ships today, `ObjectGridProps.filter` accepts `'str'`, `42`, a MongoDB-style record and a bogus rule array — all ACCEPT, with `objectName: 42` REFUSED as the discriminating control.
Not a spec bug — a release-and-floor-bump observation. Recorded so the next reader does not conclude from objectui's behaviour that the spec declined to rule.

## Dedupe words

view filter rule value shape scalar operator array comparand; ViewFilterRuleSchema superRefine checkViewFilterRuleValueShape; FILTER_TEXT_CASES icontains empty comparand parse; ObjectGridProps defaultFilters z.unknown ungated; ADR-0087 filter narrowing authored input
